One framework, your project

Tests your agent can run. Results you can inspect.

9lives pairs a native Go runner with your existing test project. Use ordinary specs first, then add the SDK or agent tools where they help.

Web / Playwright

Keep the tests you own

Run your specs with your Playwright configuration. Add named steps and bounded natural-language goals through the optional TypeScript SDK. Explicit assertions still decide whether the expected behavior happened.

Run an existing project →
Android / experimental

Test native apps with Appium

Use Appium and UiAutomator2 for Android actions and assertions, with support for Flutter-style accessibility controls. Start with the documented emulators or phone; broader device support and iOS remain planned.

A workflow for coding agents

Reproduce a failure. Check the fix.

9lives gives a coding agent execution tools. Your reviewed tests decide which behavior matters.

01

Reproduce the failure

Start with a reviewed Playwright spec and an assertion that fails on the broken application.

run_test
02

Review the change

Inspect the proposed application patch or locator repair. Keep the test’s intended behavior and assertions.

Your coding agent
03

Confirm the fix

Run the same reproduction on each Git revision in isolation. Inspect the failing result before and the passing result after.

confirm_finding · experimental
04

Challenge the test

Inject supported fetch/XHR faults and rerun. See which faults caused an assertion failure and which survived.

9l prove · experimental
A pass has a precise meaning.

A passing receipt means the test’s assertions passed and the execution report was validated. Confirmation shows the test distinguishes two revisions. A caught fault means an assertion failed under that fault. None establishes full requirement coverage.

Start locally

Run your first spec.

The Go runner uses your project’s installed Playwright and configuration. The SDK is optional. You can run ordinary specs without an AI model or QualityMax account.

Native CLI · x64 & ARM64 · Chromium qualified · Android / Appium experimental

01 / Install the CLI on macOS or Linux
curl -fsSL https://9lives.run/install.sh | sh
02 / Add the binary to PATH
export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/9lives-runner/bin:$PATH"
03 / Run one existing Playwright spec
9l run tests/checkout.spec.ts --timeout 2m --attempts 1 --format json

Replace the spec path with your own. Your project needs Playwright dependencies and browsers. Windows ZIP installation · Quickstart · Runnable example

Inside your coding agent

Connect the tools through MCP.

Native MCP exposes run, assess, heal, confirm, page inspection, and reproduction tools. Start a page check with scan_url. Use the QA skill for requirements and source provenance. Codex and Claude setup live in the agent guide.

Set up your agent →
Example / Claude Code

Optional SDK: named steps and bounded goals. Goals still need explicit assertions; goal completion is unverified.

Before the reproduction

Inspect the page. Find the next test.

One Chromium load gives nine categories of observations. inspect_page ranks controls and locators; generate_playwright_repro writes a reviewable spec for a finding.

console

JavaScript errors, warnings, and failed requests

links

Broken and redirecting links

accessibility

Alt text, control names, and heading structure

performance

LCP, CLS, TTFB, and FCP from one cold page load

seo

Page title and meta description

security_headers

CSP, HSTS, and browser security headers

cookies

Cookie flags, trackers, and tracking before consent

mixed_content

HTTP resources and forms on HTTPS pages

weight

Transfer bytes, requests, and oversized assets

Scan a public page
9l scan https://your-app.dev --format markdown

Scans are observations, not test results. Load timings are from one cold visit; INP is not measured. Authenticated pages need explicit consent, and loopback targets need --allow-private-network. Page-check guide →

Current capabilities

Choose a qualified starting point.

Available

Local execution & assessment

Plans, bounded runs, cancellation, terminal receipts, advisory static assessment, page checks, and native MCP. Existing Playwright specs stay usable.

Experimental

Healing, confirmation, fault testing & Android

Supported locator repairs are verified in isolation. Confirmation compares revisions. Fault testing challenges fetch/XHR paths. The demo qualifies one synthetic app in Chromium. Android execution uses Appium and UiAutomator2, qualified on the documented API 35 emulators and one Android 17 phone.

Planned

Broader behavioral verification

Independent behavioral verification and verified replay remain subsequent milestones, as do iOS and Android qualification beyond the documented emulators and phone. Other browser engines are unqualified.

Using the original Python package?

Python remains in maintenance mode for existing workflows, with no removal date set. Use Go for new Playwright projects. Check 9l --version when both distributions are installed.

uv tool install 9lives
